provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 70-72; antecedent printed p. 341; text-layer lines 50629-50636
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: THE 1862 TEXT LAYER HAS NO et BEFORE renova. The layer breaks the line as mentes nostras benignus, / renova coelestibus sacra-, and the word is simply not in these bytes; 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 spells coelestibus where the typica prints caelestibus; 1862 sets a comma after pariter which the typica does not. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at lines 53740-53752 prints benignus, [Tironian et] renoua celestibus sacramentis, and Vatican typica 1604 at lines 38821-38831 prints benignus, & renoua caelestibus sacramentis; both were read on the spot and both supply et at exactly this point. Recorded limitation: THE ONE REAL GAP IN THIS LANE, recorded rather than repaired. The 1862 text layer is missing the conjunction et before renova, at a line boundary, in a scan that demonstrably loses material at line boundaries -- in the already-committed pentecost-14 Collect the same layer breaks propitia-/ne and loses the syllable tio from propitiatione. Two independent tracked public-domain witnesses, the 1570 and the 1604, print et there, and I read both loci rather than resting on a grep. I have NOT repaired the 1862 reading and I have NOT read an 1862 page image, because that book's page images are registered storage = remote and this lane may not download. If the applier wants the 103(b) corroboration for this one word to rest on the 1862 alone, this oration should be held back or a checked 1570/1604 passage should be registered for it; on the 1862 alone the honest verdict for that single conjunction is unproven. RESOLVED ON 2026-09-05, AND THE CONFIDENCE RAISED FROM medium TO high. What the earlier lane could not do -- open the 1862 page image -- has been done. Internet Archive leaf n426 of item bub_gb_E7sPAAAAIAAJ = printed p. 341 is now registered on the Pustet edition as artifact.catholic-church.missale-romanum.pustet-ratisbon-1862.ia-bookreader-leaf-426-50a5e6c3, SHA-256 50a5e6c35bc4685d31ddf1aa66632fc6cb34a18422cf6ddb95d611210e9e9b43, 1,145,486 bytes, 2500 by 4097 pixels, retained in this repository under a public-domain basis and readable offline. The page reads 'Purifica, quaesumus Domine, mentes nostras benignus, et renova coelestibus sacramentis: ut consequenter et corporum praesens pariter, et futurum capiamus auxilium. Per Dominum.', with the conjunction standing at the end of the printed line immediately before the turn to renova -- exactly the position at which the text layer was already demonstrated to lose material. The 1862 therefore corroborates this Postcommunion word for word and whole, on its own page rather than on its optical layer, and the one gap in the 103(b) argument for this proper is closed. The remaining differences from the typica are transformations and not variants: coelestibus against caelestibus, j against consonantal i, a comma after pariter, and no comma after quaesumus. The collation is recorded at src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/56-sixteenth-after-pentecost/propers/verified.md. The text-layer reading is NOT amended: the layer still lacks the conjunction and this record keeps saying so, because what changed is the evidence available about the printing, not the bytes of the scan.
